newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says seven countries owe it $1.4 billion.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says seven countries owe it $1.4 billion.

text.p: Seven countries owe Iraq about $1.4 billion, Iraqi government newspapers said on Monday.
The papers, quoting a source at the Iraqi Finance Ministry, named the countries as Saudi Arabia, Syria, Bahrain, Kuwait, Somalia, the United Arab Emirates and Egypt.
Last October Iraq said its frozen assets in these countries totalled $1.3 billion. The increase since then was believed to be due to interest charges.
The Finance Ministry source was reported as saying that the money owed covered loans offered by Iraq, oil exports, official bank deposits and profits of joint Arab companies.
Iraq's assets abroad, mostly in U.S. and European banks, were impounded when it invaded Kuwait in 1990.

Baghdad has called many times for the release of its assets to enable it to buy food and medicine for its population, suffering from more than six years of trade sanctions imposed after the invasion of Kuwait. These calls have gone unheeded.
